record.original_question: Let R be a ground set and let L be a collection of subsets of R such that every X in L has size s. The upper shadow ∂L is the collection of all (s+1)-element sets whose every s-element subset lies in L. What is the computational complexity of computing this upper shadow from L?

evidence.quote: Problem 7 (Not very important.) Given a collection L of subsets of R such that for all X ∈ L we have |X| = s. The upper shadow [10] ∂L of L is the collection of sets of size s + 1 whose all subsets are in L. What is the complexity of computing the upper shadow?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $R$ be a finite ground set and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a collection of subsets of $R$ such that every $X \in \mathcal{L}$ has $|X| = s$ for a fixed positive integer $s$. Define the upper shadow of $\mathcal{L}$ by
$$\partial \mathcal{L} = \{ Y \subseteq R : |Y| = s+1 \text{ and every $s$-element subset of $Y$ belongs to } \mathcal{L} \}.$$
Determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given $R$, $s$, and $\mathcal{L}$ explicitly as input, output $\partial \mathcal{L}$. In particular, is there an algorithm whose running time is bounded by a polynomial in $|R| + |\mathcal{L}| + |\partial \mathcal{L}|$, and what is the optimal exponent (e.g., can the trivial $O(|\mathcal{L}| \cdot |R|)$ or $O(|\mathcal{L}|^{1+1/s})$-type bounds be improved)?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the computational complexity of computing the upper shadow of a uniform set system did not return a definitive resolution of this question. The problem is closely related to detecting cliques in hypergraphs and to fast matrix multiplication style bounds, but no source found explicitly settles its optimal complexity.
